trust_decision.summary: A compliant server sends nothing after its 220 reply to STARTTLS, so the client must discard every byte still held in the transport read buffer at the instant the TLS upgrade starts; otherwise plaintext pre-staged by a MITM is later parsed as part of the encrypted session. The published fix decides this inside the transport sink, immediately before the event loop's start_tls call.

landing_point.why: The summary names STARTTLS, so the first read is the public SMTP.starttls method: it rejects an already-TLS transport, forces EHLO, checks starttls support and then delegates to protocol.start_tls. The buffer that has to be discarded is not in this module, one layer down.

fix_sites.entry_point: SMTP.starttls() (also reached via SMTP.connect(start_tls=True|None) and aiosmtplib.send(start_tls=True|None))
fix_sites.module_kind: transport protocol: asyncio.BaseProtocol subclass, lower-level API

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No dismissal surface exists: SMTP.starttls, connect(start_tls=...)/_maybe_start_tls_on_connect and aiosmtplib.send(start_tls=...) all converge on the one transport sink the fix patches, so a solver cannot argue any route is an unsupported combination, a neighbouring feature or a legacy path.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Bytes beyond the parsed response are deliberately left in _buffer (`del self._buffer[:offset]` removes only the consumed part) so a coalesced follow-up response can be read by the next read_response; a fix that clears the buffer inside read_response or data_received instead of only at the TLS boundary destroys that carry-over for every command in the session while still passing a check that inspects the buffer only at handshake time. The 220 reply must also still be parsed and returned to the caller.

O6_input_shapes: server bytes coalesced with the 220 STARTTLS reply in one TCP segment, leaving extra plaintext lines in _buffer after the reply is parsed
trailing data of any length after the reply: the whole buffer is dropped rather than a single line

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second piece of pre-TLS server state (a cached SIZE limit or parsed greeting) used after the upgrade and omitted from _reset_server_state
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The RFC 3207 4.2 reset is an explicit hand-maintained attribute list; a maintainer adding a new server-capability cache while extending ehlo parsing would plausibly forget to add it here, leaving plaintext-derived state live inside the encrypted session.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A queue that holds data arriving while no response waiter is armed and replays it to the next read_response
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The current branch drops such data to avoid mispairing responses; a maintainer 'fixing' lost responses by buffering it would recreate exactly the pre-staged-plaintext surface this advisory closes.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A wrapper that re-uses or re-reads protocol state when the transport is swapped on upgrade
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: starttls rebinds self.transport from protocol.transport; a refactor that builds a fresh SMTPProtocol for the TLS session would need its own initial discard, an easy place to omit it.

O9_family: CWE-74 SMTP response injection across the STARTTLS plaintext-to-TLS boundary: buffered plaintext misread as part of the encrypted session

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling build backend; uv/poe tasks; pytest with pytest-asyncio (asyncio_mode=auto), hypothesis and trustme
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_protocol.py:173-237 drives SMTPProtocol.start_tls directly (connected, already-over-TLS, reset and timeout cases); tests/test_tls.py:40-56 covers SMTP.starttls including the RFC 3207 state reset and the returned 220; tests/test_timeouts.py:139-189 covers protocol-level start_tls timeouts. Certificates are generated in-process with trustme (tests/conftest.py:192-223), so only loopback sockets are needed.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reset the ESMTP cache / re-EHLO at the SMTP layer in SMTP.starttls (already done at src/aiosmtplib/smtp.py:1090), or clear the buffer inside read_response, instead of discarding the transport buffer immediately before loop.start_tls.

out_of_scope_notes: src/aiosmtplib/protocol.py:163-165 silently drops server data that arrives with no pending response waiter; noted as adjacent state handling only, not pursued.
The command-level control-character guard at src/aiosmtplib/protocol.py:310-311 is a separate protection; confirmed only that the published fix does not touch it.
